name: Adalo
tagline: Build a constrained PWA from a schema and fixed mobile components

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited test apps, screens and actions; 500 records/app; 1 editor; 0 published apps
tiers.notes: Build and preview only; publishing requires a paid plan.

tiers.name: Starter
tiers.limits: 1 published app; 1 editor; 5 GB team storage; unlimited app actions
tiers.notes: Annual billing is 20% lower than monthly.

tiers.name: Professional
tiers.limits: 2 published apps; 5 editors; 25 GB team storage; unlimited app actions
tiers.notes: Annual billing is 20% lower than monthly.

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: 5 published apps; 10 editors; 125 GB team storage; unlimited app actions
tiers.notes: Annual billing is 20% lower than monthly.

tiers.name: Adalo Blue
tiers.limits: Custom dedicated infrastructure, monitoring, data-source and deployment terms

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited test apps, screens and actions; 500 database records/app; 1 editor; 0 published apps
pricing.hiddenCosts: No platform usage or token overages, but app-store release requires an Apple Developer account ($99/year) and Google Play Developer account ($25 one time); premium marketplace components or external services can add cost

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Adalo, build a constrained PWA from a schema and fixed mobile components. The hard boundary is native app builds, app-store workflow, marketplace components, hosting, and support, plus connectors, runtime reliability, and governance.
coreLoopDIY: Define tables and views, build a constrained CRUD interface as a PWA from fixed mobile components, connect one approved data source, and deploy it for a small trusted team.
requirements: API credentials for one selected integration
whatYouLose: native app builds, app-store workflow, marketplace components, hosting, and support
ongoingBurden: schema migration, auth, permissions, connector drift, queues, deployments, backups, and auditability
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Adalo because the builder is only useful when its runtime, connectors, permissions, and deployments remain boring for years. The recurring cost buys schema migration, auth, permissions, connector drift, queues, deployments, backups, and auditability, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Appsmith
priorArt.desc: Large open-source low-code platform for internal applications and data sources.

alternatives.name: Glide Free
alternatives.desc: A schema-first mobile-style web app with fixed components and ten personal users; native app-store binaries are not included.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Appsmith Community
rejectedAlternatives.desc: An internal desktop-web tool builder, not a consumer-facing mobile-style PWA builder.

rejectedAlternatives.name: MIT App Inventor
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It builds Android and iOS packages, not a hosted progressive web app.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Thunkable Free
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free plan is public-project prototyping; keeping a published web or mobile app alive requires a subscription.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Starter plan and a small-team internal app DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Adalo in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and Docker Compose; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: define tables and views, build a constrained CRUD interface as a PWA from fixed mobile components, connect one approved data source, and deploy it for a small trusted team.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a schema editor for text, number, boolean, date, enum, and relation fields.
Generate list, detail, create, edit, and kanban views from the schema.
Implement role-based read and write rules for admin and member roles.
Support one REST connector with encrypted credentials and explicit field mapping.
Add an activity log, CSV import or export, backups, and health checks.
Ship Docker Compose with migrations and a seeded example workspace.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out arbitrary user-authored code execution.
Deliberately leave out a broad integration marketplace.
Deliberately leave out native mobile binaries and enterprise compliance.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
